title: Germany 5-0 Netherlands: Gruda and Wirtz shine in five-star rout
subtitle: Germany delivered arguably their best display under Jurgen Klopp as they beat the Netherlands to reach the Nations League quarter-finals.
paragraphs: Germany emphatically secured their progression to the Nations League quarter-finals as they thumped the Netherlands 5-0 to seal top spot in Group A2 on Monday.
Brajan Gruda starred with two assists and a goal at Olympiastadion, with Florian Wirtz also finding the back of the net twice, including a 60th-minute thunderbolt.
Derry Scherhant got the ball rolling with a sensational strike of his own in the first half, while Nico Schlotterbeck also got himself on the scoresheet to cap a dominant triumph.
But it was the Netherlands who spurned a glorious chance to take the lead in the 25th minute through Donyell Malen, who somehow headed Cody Gakpo's cross over the bar.

After hitting the post earlier in the half, Scherhant gave Germany the lead four minutes before the break with a superb finish. Having cut inside from the left-hand side, he rifled a sensational effort past Bart Verbruggen and into the top-right corner.
Scherhant should have doubled his tally within 57 seconds after the restart, but after seeing his initial attempt blocked, he could only fire over the crossbar on the rebound.
Denzel Dumfries headed over a glorious chance at the other end moments later, with Gakpo calling Marc ter Stegen into action with a bouncing effort that was pushed to safety.

But Germany doubled their lead on the hour through Wirtz. The Liverpool attacker pinched possession from Dumfries before cutting inside the Netherlands captain and firing a left-footed shot into the roof of the net from 25 yards out.
It got even better for Jurgen Klopp's team five minutes later when Schlotterbeck stooped down low to head in Gruda's inviting free-kick from the left into the back of the net.

Gruda was involved again for Germany's fourth goal soon after, driving at the Netherlands defence before flicking the ball back for Wirtz, who brought up his brace with a volley that kissed the crossbar on its way in.
And further gloss was added to the scoreline 13 minutes from time by Gruda, who turned in from close range after seeing Scherhant's initial shot strike the left post and bounce kindly into his path.
Despite the defeat, the Netherlands are also into the last eight of the competition despite Greece beating Serbia 1-0 thanks to Giorgos Masouras' 69th-minute strike.
Germany, the Netherlands and Greece ended on 11 points – with results between them being used as the tiebreaker instead of goal difference.
Wirtz's fine form continues as Klopp delivers statement win

Many Liverpool supporters would have hoped the appointment of Klopp at Germany would bring out the best in Wirtz, who has struggled to adapt in the Premier League thus far, but this international break has proved that when playing with confidence, he looks a completely different player.

Wirtz now has four goals and an assist in his last three matches for club and country, and he will be hoping to maintain that momentum against Manchester United this Sunday, but Gruda also deserves praise for a fine individual display.

Gruda, who is out on loan at RB Leipzig from high-flying Brighton, finished with team-high totals for touches in the opposition box (13), chances created (three) and passes in the final third (29), and Fabian Hurzeler will be watching his performances closely.

It was dominance from start to finish from Germany, who ended with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.52 from their 18 shots to the Netherlands' 1.16 from their nine attempts, though only one of those were on target.

Xavi's tenure hit its biggest bump in the road as the Netherlands went five goals behind in an international match for the first time since 1959, when they lost 7-0 to Germany, with the Spaniard left with plenty to ponder ahead of the quarter-finals.
